summary: This bill amends the Higher Education Act to require public colleges receiving federal aid to charge in-state tuition rates to U.S. nationals who reside in Guam, American Samoa, the Northern Mariana Islands, or the U.S. Virgin Islands.

scores.thoughts: The bill imposes a tuition policy requirement on public colleges receiving federal aid but does not authorize, appropriate, or alter any federal spending levels. It is a regulatory condition rather than a fiscal measure.
No provisions address tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue collection.
No provisions relate to health coverage, insurance, or medical services.
No provisions address firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.

The bill references the definition of 'national of the United States' from the Immigration and Nationality Act solely to identify eligible territorial residents who already hold that status; it neither expands nor restricts immigration pathways.
No provisions address reproductive health services or abortion access.
No provisions address military funding, defense programs, or armed forces.
No provisions address environmental regulations, climate policy, or natural resources.
No provisions address welfare programs, food assistance, or means-tested benefits.

The bill amends the Higher Education Act to require public institutions receiving federal assistance to charge in-state tuition to eligible residents of U.S. territories. This constitutes federal involvement in public higher-education pricing and expands access to affordable public postsecondary education, aligning with the negative pole of the education topic.
No provisions address controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
No provisions address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal targets.
No provisions address protections or restrictions related to LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions address foreign assistance or international aid.
No provisions address voting access, election administration, or voter ID.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No provisions address worker protections, collective bargaining, or union rights.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
